knowledge:
- key_parameters: inp=SummarizedExperiment input object containing intensity measurements ;; bg=Background intensity threshold (set to 0 for RNA-seq, or a positive value like ~30 for microarrays) ;; cores=Number of CPU cores to use for parallel processing ;; dista=Distance threshold (default 300) for segmenting position-segments by regions without significant sequencing depth ;; pen=Penalty value for dynamic programming fragmentation ;; pen_out=Outlier penalty value for dynamic programming fragmentation ;; restr=Restriction parameter for fitting ;; rm_FLT=Logical, whether to remove probes/bins where all replicates are filtered (default FALSE)
- alternatives: None mentioned. The documentation notes that standard workflows combine individual half-life values based on given genome annotation, which cannot deal with differences within a gene, whereas rifi uses an annotation-agnostic approach.
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing high-throughput rifampicin time-series data (microarray or RNA-seq) with sufficiently high time resolution to study transcription mechanics, RNA polymerase velocity, and RNA stability/half-life in bacteria.
- pitfalls: Microarray data must be carefully checked for background; running with a low background (e.g., ~30) first to check probe fits is recommended ;; If more than 30% of fits show a misfit, check raw data and background ;; Incorrect penalties can lead to a high frequency of very long segments, mini-segments (artifacts), or extremely high values, or an absence of events/outliers ;; Input IDs must be unique strand/position combinations and must not contain "|", "_", or "," ;; The first column of the assay must be "0" (time point before rifampicin addition) and cannot contain 0 or NA.

workflows.name: rifi_wrapper_workflow
workflows.intent: Run the entire rifi analysis pipeline automatically using a single wrapper function.
input: example_input_e_coli (SummarizedExperiment object containing rifampicin time-series data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load input data and GFF3 annotation file ;; 2. Run the wrapper function rifi_wrapper to execute preprocessing, fitting, penalty estimation, fragmentation, statistics, summary, and visualization.
workflows.code:
library(rifi)
data(example_input_e_coli)
Path = gzfile(system.file("extdata", "gff_e_coli.gff3.gz", package = "rifi"))
wrapper_minimal <-
  rifi_wrapper(
    inp = example_input_e_coli,
    cores = 2,
    path = Path,
    bg = 0,
    restr = 0.01
  )

workflows.name: rifi_manual_workflow
workflows.intent: Run the rifi analysis pipeline step-by-step to allow fine-tuning of preprocessing, fitting, penalties, fragmentation, and statistical testing.
input: example_input_minimal (SummarizedExperiment object containing rifampicin time-series data)
workflows.stages: 1. Check input data format ;; 2. Preprocess data (calculate means, segment positions, find PDD and TI candidates) ;; 3. Fit standard and TI models ;; 4. Perform fragmentation using dynamic programming ;; 5. Run statistical tests to identify transcription events ;; 6. Summarize results ;; 7. Visualize genome-wide fragments and events.
workflows.code:
probe <- check_input(inp = example_input_minimal, thrsh = 0)
probe <-
  make_df(
    inp = probe,
    cores = 2,
    bg = 0,
    rm_FLT = TRUE
  )
probe <- segment_pos(inp = probe, dista = 300)
probe <-
  finding_PDD(
    inp = probe,
    cores = 2,
    pen = 2,
    pen_out = 2,
    thrsh = 0.001
  )
probe <-
  finding_TI(
    inp = probe,
    cores = 2,
    pen = 10,
    thrsh = 0.001
  )
preprocess_minimal <-
  rifi_preprocess(
    inp = probe,
    cores = 2,
    bg = 0,
    rm_FLT = TRUE,
    thrsh_check = 10,
    dista = 300,
    run_PDD = TRUE
  )
data(preprocess_minimal)
suppressWarnings(fit_minimal <- rifi_fit(
  inp = preprocess_minimal,
  cores = 2,
  viz = FALSE,
  restr = 0.2,
  decay = seq(.08, 0.11, by = .02),
  delay = seq(0, 10, by = .1),
  k = seq(0.1, 1, 0.2),
  bg = 0.2,
  TI_k = seq(0, 1, by = 0.5),
  TI_decay = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.6),
  TI = seq(0, 1, by = 0.5),
  TI_delay = seq(0, 2, by = 0.5),
  TI_rest_delay = seq(0, 2, by = 0.5),
  TI_bg = 0
))
data(penalties_minimal)
fragmentation_minimal <-
  rifi_fragmentation(
    inp = penalties_minimal,
    cores = 2
  )
data(fragmentation_minimal)
Path = gzfile(system.file("extdata", "gff_e_coli.gff3.gz", package = "rifi"))
stats_minimal <- rifi_stats(inp = fragmentation_minimal, dista = 300, 
                            path = Path)
summary_minimal <- rifi_summary(stats_minimal)
rifi_visualization(
  data = stats_minimal
  )
